notes: delete-confirm-modal doesn't discriminate: both with_skill and without_skill scored 100% pass rate — all three seeded issues (unused Modal import, Button nested in an anchor, missing mobile breakpoint) are catchable by strong general engineering/accessibility judgement alone, independent of any Hearth-specific documentation.

account-summary-card is the discriminating eval (88.9% vs 55.6%): the skill's docs-verification step caught the hallucinated `shadow` prop on Card and correctly identified margin-for-spacing as Hearth's specific anti-pattern — the baseline missed the hallucinated prop entirely and mis-framed the margin usage as the *good* pattern (contrasted favourably against inline styles), since it has no way to know Hearth's own gap/justifyContent convention.

The with-skill run's one failed assertion (icon title/titleId) is an eval-authoring issue, not a real skill gap — the model gave a more nuanced answer (icon is decorative, adjacent text already conveys the same info, so default aria-hidden is correct) than the assertion's literal 'flags it as needing a fix' wording allowed for. Consider rewording that assertion before the next iteration.

With-skill runs took roughly 12x longer (1663s vs 139s mean) and used about 2.2x the tokens (112k vs 50k mean) than baseline — the added cost of live docs verification (docs-list/docs-show, including at least one retried 5xx timeout per run) against a real gain in catching hallucinated props and Hearth-specific anti-patterns that general judgement alone missed or got backwards.
